title: Jitterbug, Lionel Hampton at the Municipal Auditorium and the first electric bass
summary: He danced the jitterbug, and remembers Hampton's remark to the segregated balcony and the first electric bass in his band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So what, what, um, as, when you were dating, when you go out, what, what, what dances were popular then?

Oh, the jitterbug, jitterbug. And I was a pretty good jitterbug. Oh, wow. I danced pretty good. I danced pretty good. And, uh, we used to go to the, we used to go to the show. I remember, I remember taking my wife to see Lionel Hampton at the municipal auditorium. And I remember one comment he made, and it stands out in my mind too. You know, uh, the whites were downstairs and we were upstairs. You said generally how it was.

Yeah. Downstairs and we were upstairs. Yeah, upstairs. And Lionel Hampton said, he said, I know y'all are there. He said, I can't see you, but I can hear you. See, we were upstairs. He said, maybe one day we'll all be together. You know, but that's just a comment. And there was nothing big made out of it. Yeah. But he just, he passed that comment. And, uh, the first electronic bass in a band, I heard, was in Lionel Hampton band. And the bass player was Chuck Bader. He, you know, Chuck Bader went with Lionel Hampton. He was the first player to play electronic bass in Lionel Hampton band. And we'd hear that. I heard that bass. And boy, how good it sounded. And I didn't know it was electronic bass. But somebody pointed it out. So that's an electric bass. And it was Chuck Bader playing. Okay, so you came out of the service. And, uh, what were your options as far as what you were going to do with your life when you got out? Well, when I got out, first of all, I had to think of what I wanted to do. Um, I had this singing thing was always in the back of my mind. I would try to think of what I wanted to do. Um, I had this singing thing was always in the back of my mind.
